tools.name: jactionlint
tools.rationale: lints workflows, composite actions and `dependabot.yml` for correctness, security and policy in one binary. It is a fork of actionlint whose security rules follow the audits of zizmor, so you do not need `actionlint` or `zizmor` next to it by default. `--fix` repairs what has a mechanical fix; with `--online` it also pins tags to commit SHAs.
tools.limitations: created in October 2026 and run by one maintainer; parity with zizmor is self-reported. If you need an established second implementation, offline archived-action detection, pre-commit config audits or an LSP, add [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor).

tools.name: Plumber
tools.rationale: CI/CD security scanner for GitLab CI (and GitHub Actions): checks `.gitlab-ci.yml`, resolved includes and project settings such as branch protection, and reports to the terminal, JSON, SARIF and GitLab SAST. Runs locally, in Docker or as a GitLab CI component. The only widely adopted GitLab pipeline scanner found: 829 stars, 30 releases, v0.7.11 on 2026-10-21, MPL-2.0, used by projects such as Delve and Resty.
tools.limitations: Created 2026-01-19 and pre-1.0. A security and compliance scanner, not a syntax checker: use GitLab's own CI Lint (also `glab ci lint`) for syntax. Its exit codes were not checked here. For GitHub Actions we recommend jactionlint instead.

tools.name: Ruff
tools.rationale: linter and formatter that replaces Flake8, isort, pyupgrade and Black.
tools.limitations: no type checking, no custom-rule plugins. The `S` rules replace Bandit, `D` replaces pydocstyle (archived) and `C901` replaces xenon and radon; pair with vulture for dead code across modules.

tools.name: ty
tools.rationale: Rust-native Python type checker and language server from the authors of Ruff and uv. The most starred of the new checkers (19.9k stars) and downloaded as much as pyright (about 41 million PyPI downloads a month); v0.0.91 on 2026-10-22.
tools.limitations: Beta: 0.0.x, so new releases can add type errors; pin the version. mypy (160 million downloads) and pyright are the stable, battle-tested choices, and Pyrefly (Meta, stable 1.4, 7.1k stars) is the other Rust option.

tools.name: golangci-lint
tools.rationale: one runner for the Go linters and the formatter, with `golangci-lint custom` for your own analyzers.
tools.limitations: choose linters deliberately; GPL-3.0.

tools.name: Clippy
tools.rationale: the official linter; run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.
tools.limitations: tied to the toolchain version.

tools.name: RuboCop
tools.rationale: linter and formatter with autocorrect and custom cops.
tools.limitations: slower than native-code linters. Add the `rubocop-rails`, `rubocop-rspec` (or `rubocop-minitest`) and `rubocop-performance` plugins as needed; Standard is a wrapper and not needed.

tools.name: ShellCheck
tools.rationale: bugs and portability problems in `sh`, `bash`, `dash` and `ksh`.
tools.limitations: a stable-tool exception, last release in August 2025 with ongoing commits; no zsh. jactionlint already runs it on workflow `run:` steps.

tools.name: commitlint
tools.rationale: Enforces Conventional Commits on a message, a hook or a CI range (`--from/--to`), with shareable configs. The standard by a wide margin: 18.8k stars, about 44 million npm downloads a month, v21.2.4 on 2026-10-18. Needed if releases or changelogs are generated from commits.
tools.limitations: Requires Node. Checks format only, not whether the message is accurate. Compared on 2026-10-23 with the Rust options cocogitto (1.2k stars, last push 2026-04), convco (329 stars) and committed (185 stars, last release 2026-02): none has the adoption or the release pace, so Node remains the main cost. Python projects without Node can use commitizen.

tools.name: lychee
tools.rationale: broken links.
tools.limitations: network flakiness; give it a GitHub token and a cache.

tools.name: typos
tools.rationale: low-noise spell checking of source code and docs.
tools.limitations: finds only known misspellings.

tools.name: prek
tools.rationale: Single-binary Rust runner that is a drop-in for `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and the pre-commit hook ecosystem, with monorepo workspaces. Chosen over pre-commit and hk: 8.7k stars and about 16 million PyPI downloads a month against hk's 1.3k stars; v0.5.7 on 2026-10-21.
tools.limitations: Pre-1.0. Hooks can be bypassed (`--no-verify`), so run the same checks in CI. hk (jdx) is the other Rust runner and fits mise-based projects; pre-commit (15.7k stars) is the conservative fallback.

tools.name: Knip
tools.rationale: unused files, exports and dependencies.
tools.limitations: monorepos need configuration; never run `--fix` unattended.

tools.name: deptry
tools.rationale: unused, missing and transitive dependencies.
tools.limitations: static analysis misses dynamic imports.

tools.name: ast-grep
tools.rationale: project-specific syntax rules as YAML, with tests for the rules themselves (`ast-grep test`).
tools.limitations: syntax only, no data-flow analysis.

tools.name: database_consistency
tools.rationale: Ruby and Rails: compares ActiveRecord models with the database schema and reports missing null constraints, foreign keys and unique indexes, redundant indexes, mismatched enums and key types, and broken associations (20+ checkers). The established tool of its kind: v3.1.1 on 2026-10-22, 4.3 million gem downloads, MIT, supported by Pennylane.
tools.limitations: ActiveRecord only. Its exit code and machine-readable output were not checked. Go projects can use schemalens, which is modelled on it.

tools.name: schemalens
tools.rationale: compares a Go model (ent, gorm, bun) with the live PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite schema and reports every disagreement as a structured finding, with JSON and SARIF output, a baseline and an agent skill. Checks things a structural diff does not: missing foreign-key indexes, constraints the model assumes but the database does not enforce, nullable columns for required fields.
tools.limitations: **maintained by the owner of this repository**; created 2026-10-20, v0.1.x, one maintainer, no outside users yet. Go models only. Compared with database_consistency (the Ruby original, listed above) and Atlas (structural diff and drift, a different job); no Go equivalent was found.

tools.name: Oxlint and oxfmt
tools.rationale: Rust-native linter and formatter from the Oxc toolchain: Oxlint runs ESLint-compatible rules (type-aware ones need TypeScript 7), oxfmt is the Prettier-compatible formatter. One fast toolchain instead of ESLint plus Prettier; releases weekly (oxlint 1.89, oxfmt 0.74 on 2026-10-19).
tools.limitations: oxfmt is pre-1.0. Oxlint exits 0 on warnings, so pass `--deny-warnings` in CI (tested). Per its docs, Vue, Svelte and Angular template files are not linted and the plugin ecosystem is smaller than ESLint's: keep ESLint only where you depend on those.

tools.name: TypeScript
tools.rationale: `tsc --noEmit` with `strict`; version 7 is the native, much faster compiler.
tools.limitations: the TypeScript 7 compiler API is not ready, so tools that import `typescript` may need TypeScript 6 beside it. `microsoft/typescript-go` is archived because it was merged, not abandoned.

tools.name: dependency-cruiser
tools.rationale: import-graph rules (forbidden paths, cycles, orphans, dev-deps in production code) with non-zero exit and JSON output; `--ignore-known` baselines legacy violations. Chosen over eslint-plugin-boundaries because it does not depend on the lint stack.
tools.limitations: static analysis misses dynamic imports; no autofix.

tools.name: Betterleaks
tools.rationale: finds committed secrets in files, git history and pull requests, with optional live validation of credentials. Chosen over Gitleaks because it reads the same kind of TOML rules and `gitleaks:allow` comments and is still released, while Gitleaks has had no release since March 2026 (v8.30.1). Its README says it is maintained by the people behind Gitleaks.
tools.limitations: created February 2026; the stable line is v1.9.0 while v2 is in release-candidate, so pin the version; recall claims are the project's own; TruffleHog (AGPL-3.0) and Kingfisher (Apache-2.0) are the alternatives.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.rationale: known vulnerabilities in lockfiles and SBOMs across many ecosystems, with call analysis to reduce noise.
tools.limitations: not an image scanner; if you scan container images use Trivy (never `trivy-action` by tag, pin to a version or digest after the March 2026 compromise) or Grype.

tools.name: Renovate
tools.rationale: Dependency update bot that works on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea and Forgejo, where Dependabot is GitHub-only. Policy lives in one config: pinning, grouping, and `minimumReleaseAge` to hold back freshly published versions. `renovate-config-validator` checks the config in CI. The most used of its kind: 22.8k stars, v44.181.0 on 2026-10-23, 1.7 million npm downloads a month.
tools.limitations: An update bot, not a gate: it opens pull requests and fails nothing by itself, so pair it with CI checks. AGPL-3.0 (using it, hosted or self-hosted, is fine; modifying and offering it as a service is not). Configuration is large; start from a shared preset. Dependabot is enough for a GitHub-only repository.

tools.name: Hadolint
tools.rationale: Dockerfile best practices.
tools.limitations: GPL-3.0; security-focused IaC checks belong to Trivy or Checkov.

tools.name: TFLint
tools.rationale: Terraform correctness and provider-specific rules through plugins.
tools.limitations: `tflint --init` downloads plugins, so pin them; for IaC security add Trivy `config` (if you already run Trivy) or Checkov (no clear winner).

tools.name: Kubeconform
tools.rationale: validates Kubernetes manifests against API and CRD schemas.
tools.limitations: validity only; last release June 2026.

tools.name: check-jsonschema
tools.rationale: validates YAML, JSON and TOML against JSON Schema, with ready hooks for common formats.
tools.limitations: mostly a one-maintainer project; remote schemas need network or vendoring; style rules need yamllint.

tools.name: squawk
tools.rationale: finds PostgreSQL migrations that lock tables or cause downtime, with JSON output and no database needed.
tools.limitations: PostgreSQL only, no autofix; SQLFluff covers style. Atlas lint is not adopted: its stronger checks need Atlas Pro and a login.

tools.name: Conftest
tools.rationale: your own rules in Rego over YAML, JSON, HCL, Dockerfile, CODEOWNERS and 15 more formats.
tools.limitations: Rego is harder to write than YAML rules; exit code and SARIF output were not verified. Kyverno is for Kubernetes admission only.

tools.name: agnix
tools.rationale: lints CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hooks and MCP configs for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode and Kiro, with `--fix`. Tested: errors exit 1; warnings exit 0 unless `--strict` is passed.
tools.limitations: created January 2026, one main maintainer; rules track fast-changing vendor formats.

tools.name: govulncheck
tools.rationale: reports known vulnerabilities in the Go modules and standard library you actually call, with call stacks, from the official Go vulnerability database.
tools.limitations: with `-json` and `-format sarif` it exits 0 whatever it finds, so gate on the text output; blind to calls through `reflect`; the GitHub repo is a mirror of `golang.org/x/vuln`. For repos in several languages see the open Vulnerabilities decision.

tools.name: rustfmt
tools.rationale: the official formatter; run `cargo fmt --check` in CI.
tools.limitations: versioned with the Rust toolchain, not through GitHub releases; style options are few by design.

tools.name: cargo-machete
tools.rationale: Finds unused dependencies in Cargo.toml quickly and without compiling, so it runs on stable Rust in CI. The most used of the three tools compared (1.4k stars; cargo-udeps 2.1k stars needs nightly, cargo-shear 577).
tools.limitations: Text-based search, so it can report false positives and misses macro-generated uses; ignore them in Cargo.toml metadata. Not a replacement for cargo-deny, which covers advisories and licences.

tools.name: cargo-deny
tools.rationale: one policy file for RustSec advisories, licences, banned or duplicate crates and allowed registries; non-zero exit on violation. It replaces `cargo-audit` for the advisory check.
tools.limitations: checks metadata only, not dependency source; needs a maintained `deny.toml`.

tools.name: Error Prone
tools.rationale: bug patterns checked by the Java compiler on every build; raise a check to `ERROR` to fail the build. With [NullAway](https://github.com/uber/NullAway) as a plugin it also enforces null safety from `@Nullable` annotations.
tools.limitations: Java only; must run on JDK 21 or newer (it can still target older releases); NullAway needs annotations.

tools.name: Spotless
tools.rationale: `spotlessCheck` fails on unformatted code and `spotlessApply` fixes it; wraps google-java-format, ktlint, ktfmt and others behind one Gradle or Maven task.
tools.limitations: a build-tool plugin, not a standalone binary.

tools.name: ArchUnit
tools.rationale: layers, cycles and naming rules written as JUnit tests; a violated rule fails the test run.
tools.limitations: a library inside your test suite; works on bytecode, so it has no source-level rules.

tools.name: .NET SDK analyzers
tools.rationale: built in, no extra package. Set `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`, `AnalysisMode`, `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, and make NuGet Audit warnings NU1903 and NU1904 errors for vulnerable packages.
tools.limitations: rule sets change with SDK versions, so pin `AnalysisLevel`; audit data comes from the GitHub Advisory Database.

tools.name: SwiftLint
tools.rationale: style and convention rules built on SwiftSyntax; `--strict` fails on warnings, `--fix` corrects, SARIF/JSON/GitHub reporters, custom rules in config.
tools.limitations: it is a linter, not a formatter; pair with `swift-format` or SwiftFormat if you want enforced layout.

tools.name: import-linter
tools.rationale: import contracts (layers, forbidden, independence, protected) that fail CI.
tools.limitations: checks imports only; [tach](https://github.com/tach-org/tach) is the alternative for public-interface rules.

tools.name: Mago
tools.rationale: Rust-native PHP toolchain: linter, formatter, static analyzer and architectural `guard` rules in one binary, with auto-fixes and a baseline. Replaces PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer and Deptrac; 30 releases, v1.58.2 on 2026-10-19.
tools.limitations: Created in October 2024, so younger than PHPStan; its framework-specific extensions (Laravel, Symfony) were not compared rule by rule. Check your framework's coverage before dropping PHPStan.

tools.name: rumdl
tools.rationale: Rust-native Markdown linter and formatter that reads markdownlint configuration, so migration is cheap. `rumdl check` exits 1 on violations, `rumdl fmt` fixes; has a GitHub Action. Chosen over markdownlint-cli2 as the fast single-binary option.
tools.limitations: Pre-1.0 (v0.3.0). Compatibility with markdownlint is the project's own claim; custom JavaScript rules written for markdownlint are not expected to carry over.

tools.name: oasdiff
tools.rationale: Compares two OpenAPI specs and reports the changes that break existing API clients (`breaking`) or all consumer-visible changes (`changelog`), with a GitHub Action and a pre-commit hook. The standard backward-compatibility check for OpenAPI: 1.4k stars, v1.34.1 on 2026-10-21, Apache-2.0; rules are customizable.
tools.limitations: OpenAPI only (use Buf for protobuf). The exact option that makes CI fail on breaking changes was not checked here; read its docs. pb33f's openapi-changes is the smaller alternative.

tools.name: vacuum
tools.rationale: Single-binary linter for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Arazzo and JSON Schema that reads Spectral-style rulesets, so existing rules carry over. Chosen over Spectral and Redocly CLI as the fast native option with no Node dependency; v0.35.1 on 2026-10-23, MIT.
tools.limitations: Smaller community than Spectral (1.1k against 3.2k stars; Spectral and Redocly CLI each have 7 to 10 million npm downloads a month). Spectral compatibility has documented limits (see its README). Exits 2 when a rule times out, so incomplete runs are visible.

tools.name: Buf
tools.rationale: Protobuf lint, format and breaking-change detection against a previous version or git ref, in one CLI. The de facto standard for protobuf: 11.5k stars, v1.75.0 on 2026-10-22, Apache-2.0.
tools.limitations: Protobuf only. The Buf Schema Registry is an optional hosted service; lint and breaking-change checks run locally against a git ref.

tools.name: sqruff
tools.rationale: Rust-native SQL linter and formatter with SQLFluff-style rules, a `--dialect` per project and autofix. Chosen over SQLFluff as the fast single binary; v0.43.0 on 2026-10-22, Apache-2.0.
tools.limitations: Pre-1.0 and far smaller than SQLFluff (1.4k against 10k stars, 9 million PyPI downloads a month). Check your dialect before switching, and keep SQLFluff if you need its dbt and Jinja templating. Style only: use squawk for migration safety.
